exposure: Type of cooking fuel (firewood/kerosene vs. ethanol stoves)
outcome: Fetal biometric parameters (ultrasound estimated fetal weight, head circumference, abdominal circumference, femur length, biparietal diameter, estimated gestational age, intrauterine growth restriction)
Birth anthropometric measures (birth weight, birth length)
cohort: The study included 324 pregnant Nigerian women who customarily cooked with polluting fuels (firewood or kerosene).
finding: Prenatal maternal psychological distress (PMPD) negatively impacted fetal biometric parameters (ultrasound estimated fetal weight, head circumference, femur length, biparietal diameter) and birth length, acting as an independent mediator of adverse fetal biometric parameters in women exposed to household air pollution.
